title: API authentication: key, token, JWT and OAuth

videos.script: Every request to a protected API has to answer one question first. Who is asking? {{who}} This lesson tests the answers boxoffice accepts. There are three kinds. {{kinds}} The first is a key, a fixed secret for a program. The theatre's staff report uses one. {{key}} The second is a token. A program trades its credentials for it, and the token expires. {{token}} boxoffice's tokens are JWTs. You will open one and read what is inside, and then change it and watch the server refuse. {{jwt}} Then the difference between two refusals. A 401 means the server does not know you. A 403 means it knows you, and the answer is no. {{codes}} Apps on a phone sign people in another way, with OAuth and a code challenge. boxoffice does not have it, so you will see the sequence and what a tester checks. {{oauth}} And last, where secrets live, and the places they leak. {{secrets}} By the end, you can test that an API lets in what it should, and nothing else.
